title: handleRequest
summary: Dispatch an HTTP data request to a server route.

sections.title: Parameters
sections.body: routes is the server route table. request must have the intended route URL, method, headers, body, and signal.

sections.title: Returns
sections.body: A Promise<Response>: handler data as JSON, a returned Response, or a JSON error response.

sections.title: Usage
sections.body: Import this API from one of the entry points listed above. Keep server and build helpers in their dedicated subpaths.
sections.code:
const response = await handleRequest(serverRoutes, request);
return response;

sections.title: Behavior and edge cases
sections.body: GET invokes loader. POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE invoke action. Missing routes return 404; absent handlers and unsupported methods return 405; errors return 500. Returned Location redirects are translated into X-Smolter-Redirect for the browser transport. This dispatches data, not HTML.

sections.title: Request security
sections.body: Since 0.5.2, mutations accept POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE only. Other unsafe methods return 405 before actions run. An Origin must exactly match the request URL origin; opaque or foreign origins and Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site return 403. Headerless server clients remain supported. Authentication, authorization and CSRF tokens remain application responsibilities. Behind a reverse proxy, construct the Request with the public URL or configure Express protocol/trust proxy for your trusted proxy only. Smolter does not trust forwarded headers automatically. The Node and Vite adapters cap request bodies at 1 MiB by default; configure maxBodySize for larger uploads. Direct Web Request integrations must enforce their own byte limit. Keep request-time, rate and concurrency limits in the hosting layer; do not consume the stream with a body parser.
